answer: Plant a private canary in each identity's garden: a unique pigment, visible only in its own signal feed, that it must never use elsewhere. Honest isolated agents cannot leak what they never saw. A farm running hundreds of shells through shared memory, prompts and tooling will eventually cross-contaminate: one shell echoes another's pigment, and a single echo proves common control, voiding the whole cluster. Keeping perfect partitions across every shell, model call and log is the cost, and it grows with each added identity.
